findings.text: Decimal conversion routine accepts a destination buffer with capacity, an unsigned value and a requested minimum width, stages digits in an aligned scratch area with direct handling for single-symbol values and helper delegation otherwise, emits blank padding followed by decimal digits, and reports total output length while signalling overflow with an empty result.

Formatting flag mask uses distinct single-bit values with signed handling at 1 [CITED], left justification at 2 [CITED], explicit plus at 4 [CITED], blank sign at 8 [CITED], zero padding at 16 [CITED], small hex at 32 [CITED] and special prefix at 64 [CITED], where zero padding matches blank-to-zero distance and small matches case-bit distance.
Format parser distinguishes plain text, numeric, width, precision, character, string, pointer, escaped percent and invalid states, allowing the scanner to dispatch each conversion phase separately.

Conversion descriptor holds flag bits and numeric base as narrow unsigned bytes, digit or character limit as a short signed count, and output field width as a signed integer, stored without inter-field padding.
Field width ceiling equals 1 [CITED] left-shifted by 23 [CITED] then decremented by 1 [CITED], while precision ceiling equals 1 [CITED] left-shifted by 15 [CITED] then decremented by 1 [CITED].

Early boot option handler enables a weak-hash debugging flag, records enablement persistently for later read-only access after initialization, emits an informational notice and reports successful handling.

Pointer anonymization entry accepts an opaque address and an output slot, returns a busy failure while the secret remains unseeded, otherwise stores a shortened stable identifier derived from keyed hashing with explicit narrowing on wide builds and reports success.
Subsystem initialization hook registers a random-seed notifier that fills the pointer-hash secret from the kernel entropy source exactly once during early bring-up.

Pointer-hash secret publication orders the key store before the readiness flag store, while readers sample the flag with single-access semantics before sampling the key with an acquire barrier, preventing use of uninitialized secrets.
Pointer exposure restriction level lives in a read-mostly integer that is expected to remain stable during steady-state operation after early configuration.

Formatting presets provide a plain string profile, a hexadecimal flag profile with prefix and lowercase handling, a plain decimal profile, and narrow fixed-width zero-padded decimal profiles for short counters.

String preset uses width minus 1 [CITED] with precision minus 1 [CITED], flag preset uses base 16 [CITED] with precision minus 1 [CITED], decimal preset uses base 10 [CITED] with precision minus 1 [CITED], two-wide preset uses base 10 [CITED] with width 2 [CITED] and precision minus 1 [CITED], four-wide preset uses base 10 [CITED] with width 4 [CITED] and precision minus 1 [CITED]. Flag preset combines special prefix with lowercase handling while wide presets request zero padding.

Page flag descriptor groups bit-field width, shift and mask as signed integers with a formatting preset pointer and a human-readable name pointer, instantiated as a static table covering section, node, zone, last CPU identifier and sanitizer tag entries.

Pointer hashing policy cycles among always hash, never hash and automatic selection, where finalization resolves automatic mode from a debugging indicator and disabled hashing triggers a prominent multi-line security notice.

Boot command handlers accept auto alongside never and always spellings with fallback to automatic mode on empty or unrecognized input, while a legacy compatibility handler forces persistent unhashed operation.
Format cursor bundles a remaining-input pointer with a parser phase tag and a numeric size indicator for integer promotions.
Unbounded string formatter forwards its destination, template and variadic arguments to a bounded engine using a very large capacity limit.

Binary formatter walks a template once, storing each variadic datum into a word-aligned output area with per-type alignment and capacity checks, expanding strings inline and resolving certain pointer forms immediately while deferring other pointer values for later rendering.

Binary encoding truncates safely when capacity exhausts, guarantees nul termination of emitted pointer text even at the boundary, aborts cleanly on invalid conversions and preserves alignment of the final word count.

Binary encoding dispatch treats plain text and escaped percent as no-ops, width and precision as integer consumptions with special handling before pointer forms, and separates character and string and pointer and numeric paths with alphanumeric suffix skipping after pointer forms.

Sliding-window extreme tracker retains a trio of timestamped candidates ordered by recency and value, resetting fully on a new extreme or total window expiry and otherwise promoting secondary choices before reporting the current extreme.

Window aging shifts choices forward when the newest sample falls outside the full interval, captures a fresh middle choice after a quarter interval of stability, and captures a fresh trailing choice after a half interval of stability.
Distinguished array marker uses a non-null pointer value with numeric address 1 [CITED] to denote deferred reclamation state.

Split-order helper rounds a requested order downward to a chunk-aligned boundary, stepping back by one when already aligned except for preserving zero, otherwise subtracting the intra-chunk remainder.

Array cursor stepping adjusts the logical index unless frozen, delegates empty and non-node positions to boundary and load helpers, climbs toward ancestors on offset wrap and descends through interior nodes until reaching a consumable entry.

Conditional array update exchanges an expected old entry for a new entry with allocation retry, normalizing absent entries and zero markers, while insertion reports busy when occupancy already exists and propagates allocation failures.

Raw conditional update rejects advanced entries, retries transparently across transient allocation shortages, and clears the free-tracking mark when transitioning from empty to occupied under tracking configurations.
Mark clearing pairs an unlocked worker that acts only on present entries with a locked wrapper that serializes the same worker under array lock protection.
Bulk extraction holds a read-side critical section across iteration, skipping transient retry markers and stopping at an upper bound or a caller-supplied capacity.

Array harvest routine copies present or marked entries into caller storage up to a requested limit, selecting marked iteration only when the filter denotes a valid mark and returning the harvested count with immediate success on empty requests.

Diagnostic dump traverses array structure recursively, distinguishing nested nodes from values and direct pointers and retry and sibling and zero markers while annotating each level with index context and flag and mark summaries.

Narrow non-cryptographic hash seeds four lanes for longer inputs with striped accumulation and lane fusion, otherwise seeds directly, then absorbs trailing words and bytes with prime mixing and length addition before a final avalanche.

Wide non-cryptographic hash seeds four lanes for longer inputs with striped accumulation and merging, otherwise seeds directly, then absorbs trailing wide words with folding plus an optional narrow word and remaining bytes before length addition and a final avalanche.
Wide streaming reset clears the state area then installs lane seeds derived from the supplied seed combined with leading wide primes.
